newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher on U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher on U.S. data.

text.p: Swedish shares rebounded to end higher on Thursday, lifted by higher-than-expected U.S. jobless claims data.
The exchange's general index rose 0.61 percent to 2,506.89 after share worth 4.29 billion crowns changed hands.
Heavyweights drugs company Astra and telecoms group Ericsson supported the index with steady rises. Astra rose 5.5 crowns to 342.5 while Ericsson gained two to 235 crowns.
Fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz, car safety equipment group Autoliv and forestry company SCA released annual earnings. The figures lifted H&M but knocked the others.
H&M rose 18 to 1,109, while Autoliv fell five to 315 and SCA fell one crown to 143 crowns.
"Expectations were high ahead of (H&M's) report and they were largely met," a trader said. "But the question is what happens now. The share is doubtless trading at high levels."
Among winners were automotive group Volvo, which rose 1.5 to 174 crowns.
The New York bourse will decide Friday trends, dealers said.
